articles.title: Czech Darts Open: Luke Humphries knocks out Beau Greaves as Luke Littler and Michael van Gerwen also win
articles.summary: World No 1 Luke Littler won on his return to European Tour action for the first time since March; Beau Greaves' tournament is over after making history on Friday by becoming the first woman in history to win on the European Tour
articles.body:
Luke Littler also won on his return to the European Tour in Prague, while there were round two wins for Michael van Gerwen, Gian van Veen and Gerwyn Price.

However, Stephen Bunting suffered defeat to Luke Woodhouse in the final match of the day.

After Greaves became the first woman ever to win on the European Tour stage on Friday, Humphries ended the hopes of the young star, averaging just shy of 109 to book his place in the last 16.

Greaves opened the contest with a 13-dart leg, before the world No 2 responded with legs of 12 and 14 of his own to lead early on.

The resilience of the three-time Women's World Matchplay champion showed, as she closed the gap to just one with her second leg of the contest, before Humphries rattled off three consecutive legs to seal the victory.

Humphries said: "She's an amazing player, she pushed me all the way, it was a couple of bits towards the end of the match that got me through in the end.

"She's just a great dart player. If I had lost today, I wouldn't have been disgraced, I would have lost to a really great dart player."

Andrew Gilding will face off with Humphries on Sunday afternoon, as the former UK Open champion dispatched of Nathan Aspinall 6-2.

Littler's return to the European Tour stage was an impressive one, as he beat Germany's Niko Springer with a stunning 108.59 average.

The world No 1, who was making his first big stage appearance since retaining the coveted World Matchplay title, raced into the final day of action, winning 6-4 and setting up a contest with Krzysztof Ratajski, who beat Jermaine Wattimena 6-2 in the opening game of the day.

Van Veen ran away a 6-1 victor over Jeffrey De Graaf and will lock horns with Ross Smith in round three, as last week's Hungarian Darts Trophy winner looks to go back-to-back on the European Tour stage, after beating Stephen Burton 6-1.

Welsh duo Jonny Clayton and Price also advanced to the final day in Prague, as the pair beat Damon Heta and Callan Rydz respectively.

Price will face off with Cameron Menzies after the Scotsman beat compatriot Gary Anderson 6-3, while Clayton will take on Keane Barry, who reached the final day with a 6-4 victory over the seeded Chris Dobey.

Van Gerwen's bid for a maiden Czech Darts Open title continues, as he moved into round three with a 6-4 victory over Mario Vandenbogaerde. He will now face fellow Dutchman Wessel Nijman in one of the standout ties of the afternoon.

Nijman fought off Martin Schindler in the final game of Saturday's afternoon session, as the German pinned a brilliant 170 checkout, before missing a crucial big number in the decider to allow Nijman to snatch victory.

Northern Irishman Josh Rock will do battle with Irishman William O'Connor, as the pair beat Ryan Joyce and Ryan Searle respectively to book their places in round three.

Luke Woodhouse closed off the evening's proceedings with a brilliant 6-4 success against Bunting, as he averaged upwards of 105 on his way to victory and will take on Dutchman Danny Noppert after his 6-1 victory over Kevin Doets.

The tournament continues with the last 16 on Sunday afternoon, followed by the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final in a bumper evening session.

articles.title: Urban Meyer: Why Big Ten, Not SEC, Is College Football's Best Conference
articles.summary: Has the Big Ten officially overtaken the SEC as the best conference in college football? Urban Meyer has the answer.
articles.body: Is the Big Ten or the SEC the best conference in college football? Urban Meyer has coached and won national championships in both conferences. And when it comes to which one is better, he has a pretty definitive answer. "For close to 20 years, the SEC, we all knew it, dominated the country and the Big Ten Conference," Meyer said on Week 1's edition of "Big Noon Kickoff" when asked about the Big Ten vs. SEC debate. "They won 13 of 17 national championships. You know what? That all changed three years ago when the Michigan Wolverines, then the Ohio State Buckeyes, and then the Indiana Hoosiers won the national title."It's not just at the top of the league. Yes, the Big Ten is 4-0 against the SEC in College Football Playoff games, but they've also won four of five in the non-College Football Playoff bowls. So, as of now, it is the best conference." That debate goes beyond results on the field. "The SEC has dominated the NFL Draft for so many years," Meyer added. "You know what happened last year? The Big Ten had more first-round picks than the SEC. The Big Ten Conference is the strongest conference in college football. That was last year. We'll see [what happens] this year." The Big Ten sent four teams to the 2024 College Football Playoff, which was the first year of the 12-team format. Then, last season (2025), it sent three teams to the playoff, with Indiana and Ohio State each earning first-round byes as the No. 1 and 2 seeds, respectively. The Big Ten also had two teams reach the semifinal round: eventual-champion Indiana and the Oregon Ducks. As for the NFL Draft, Indiana quarterback Fernando Mendoza was selected by the Las Vegas Raiders with the No. 1 pick, marking the first time a Big Ten player was selected with the top overall pick since Michigan offensive tackle Jake Long was taken by the Miami Dolphins in 2008. Even more, four of the top-10 selections in the draft were players from the Big Ten: Mendoza, Ohio State wide receiver Carnell Tate (No. 4) and Ohio State linebackers Arvell Reese (No. 5) and Sonny Styles (No. 7). Before 2023, a Big Ten team hadn't won the national championship since Ohio State captured the title in 2014 with Meyer as head coach, his third season in Columbus. Over Meyer's seven seasons at Ohio State (2012-18), the Buckeyes went a combined 83-9, winning at least 10 games in every season. Meyer's SEC coaching stint came at Florida, where he served as head coach from 2005-10. Across six seasons in Gainesville, Meyer went 65-15, won two SEC titles and captured two national championships, in 2006 and 2008. Entering Week 1 of the 2026 season, the Big Ten has three teams ranked in the top 10 of the AP Top 25 and eight teams in the Top 25 altogether: Ohio State (one), Oregon (two), Indiana (six), USC (T-14), Michigan (16), Washington (17), Penn State (18) and Iowa (22).

articles.title: ‘Full of Hate and Envy’ — WNBA Legends Ignoring Caitlin Clark’s Dominant World Cup Outing vs. China Sparks Outrage
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark gave Team USA plenty to celebrate in its opening FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup game against China. She delivered a double-double and earned...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark gave Team USA plenty to celebrate in its opening FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup game against China. She delivered a double-double and earned Player of the Game honors in a dominant 94-61 victory.

However, a postgame discussion that highlighted several Team USA veterans without mentioning Clark drew criticism from some of her supporters online.

Fans Blast Tina Charles and Renee Montgomery Over Caitlin Clark Snub

During a discussion about Team USA's victory, Charles and Montgomery highlighted the impact of several veterans, with Jackie Young receiving particular praise. Clark, however, was not mentioned despite being named Player of the Game.

The discussion quickly drew criticism from Clark supporters on X. One fan wrote

"Caitlin rises despite their disrespect. every record she breaks, every time she shines shows everyone just how irrelevant the bias media is. We know who Caitlin is and what she brings to the game and they hate her for it."

Another supporter asked, "Hey @tinacharles31 & @ReneeMontgomery, how does it feel to be full of hate and envy?"

One fan also accused the former WNBA players of being jealous of Clark's popularity, writing

"Theyre jealous of her popularity. Instead of focusing how much Caitlin has benefited the entire W, they show their pettiness. I don't even know who these women are. Before CC, the W was not even on the map. Englebert should have prepared them. Read Christine Brennan's book."

Another fan focused on Clark's performance and the recognition she received outside the United States

"I think Caitlin Clark should go to Europe and play. The refs like her. We'll see what happens. If I was her, I won't sign for long terms in WNBA. Do it only yr to yr basis. Go to Europe."

Monet Asturias took the criticism further, arguing that Clark's contributions to the league have been overlooked:

"I'm not surprised. They don't want to give the white girl props. Everyone else can see it. That's why y'all hated. After what she did for the league, more money, more jersey sales, charter flights, more media exposure & still bunch of haters."

Another fan claimed that Clark was the best player on the pitch

"CC was the best player of the game and she's starting on the bench. It is like telling MJ or Steph to take a seat."

Another supporter said they were unsurprised by the discussion, writing:

"Didn't expect anything else from those two. When it comes to people associated with the activists in the WNBA, I'm shocked when they don't twist themselves into a pretzel trying to avoid saying positive things about Caitlin Clark."

The reactions show how strongly Clark's supporters felt about her absence from the conversation. While the fans' accusations are their own opinions, the debate has added another layer to the attention surrounding Clark's Team USA performances.

articles.title: Why Did Ohio State Have Senior Day In Week 1 Against Ball State?
articles.summary: Ohio State had its Senior Day celebration prior to its 2026 season opener against Ball State, an unconventional move.
articles.body: It's the first full week of the college football season, which means it's time to honor the seniors who are playing in their final home game. Wait, what? The No. 1 AP ranked Ohio State Buckeyes held their Senior Day celebration prior to the 2026 season opener against the Ball State Cardinals on Saturday afternoon. But Senior Day usually takes place in a team's last home game of the season. Ohio State moved its Senior Day ceremony from the home finale against the Michigan Wolverines on Nov. 28 to the home opener against Ball State Saturday because its 2024 Senior Day was clouded by the Buckeyes and Wolverines getting into a post-game scuffle that involved law enforcement after Michigan tried to plant a team flag at midfield of Ohio Stadium. "We talked about it and had long conversations about [moving Senior Day]. The traditions at Ohio State here are significant and very strong and something that we all respect. When we look at all the things that go on that weekend [Michigan week], the way things have changed, there are some things that we thought about," head coach Ryan Day said in August about moving the Senior Day celebration. "The more distractions we have, there's already enough distractions that week. This was just one more thing that we could move." Ohio State recognized 31 seniors on Saturday afternoon. Elsewhere, Ohio State inducted former head coach Jim Tressel into the program's Ring of Honor. Tressel was Ohio State's head coach from 2001-10, with the Buckeyes winning the 2002 BCS championship, going a combined 106-22 and posting eight double-digit-winning seasons with him as head coach. He's also third in program history among coaches with 106 wins and fourth with an 82.8% winning percentage. Tressel is just the third coach (Woody Hayes and Paul Brown being the other two) and 10th person altogether to be put in the Buckeyes' Ring of Honor.

articles.title: El impresionante ataque de Santiago Buitrago que rozó la victoria en la Vuelta a España
articles.standfirst: Santiago Buitrago hoy: segundo puesto en la etapa 14 de la Vuelta a España 2026
articles.summary: Santiago Buitrago hoy: segundo puesto en la etapa 14 de la Vuelta a España 2026
articles.body: El ciclista colombiano Santiago Buitrago volvió a ser gran protagonista en carreteras españolas al firmar una destacada actuación en la etapa 14 de la Vuelta a España. Tras un recorrido exigente de alta montaña con final en el temido ascenso a la Sierra de La Pandera, el escarabajo nacional cruzó la meta en la segunda posición, rozando la victoria de etapa y consolidando con autoridad su maillot de líder de la clasificación de la montaña. La jornada estuvo marcada por una intensa batalla desde los primeros kilómetros, donde Buitrago se filtró en la escapada del día con el objetivo claro de sumar unidades para defender y ampliar su ventaja en el apartado de los premios de montaña. El tramo final, con los desafiantes 11 kilómetros de subida a La Pandera y rampas de alta exigencia, puso a prueba las piernas de los favoritos y de los aventureros del día. A falta de tres kilómetros para la línea de meta, Buitrago soltó un potente ataque en solitario para buscar el triunfo parcial. Sin embargo, en los metros decisivos, el alemán Marco Brenner (Tudor Pro Cycling Team) logró conectar, sobrepasar al colombiano y quedarse con la victoria de la fracción. A pesar de las altas temperaturas y el viento en contra que complicó los intentos postreros, Buitrago reconoció el esfuerzo y el nivel de su rival, mostrando optimismo de cara a lo que resta de la competencia. “Es duro. Al final quería ganar la etapa. Hoy perdí y estuve muy cerca. Pero es eso, había un corredor más fuerte, que es Brenner, y lo felicito, y por mi parte, a seguir luchando”, expresó el pedalista nacional al término de la jornada. Con este valioso segundo puesto, Buitrago ratifica su dominio absoluto en la clasificación de la montaña, alcanzando un total de 69 puntos, lo que le otorga una cómoda ventaja de 29 unidades sobre su más cercano perseguidor, el belga Wout van Aert. Entre tanto, la batalla por la clasificación general también dejó movimientos importantes: el español Enric Mas (Movistar Team) defendió con éxito el maillot rojo de líder frente a los embates de sus principales rivales, mientras que la carrera se prepara para una nueva y emocionante prueba de alta montaña este domingo en la etapa 15.

articles.title: What Is Targeting? College Football's Most Controversial Rule, Explained
articles.summary: Here's everything you need to know about targeting and its new penalty changes.
articles.body: Despite some tweaks this year, college football's most controversial rule — targeting — is still in the rulebook, and that means it's surely going to create some confusion and frustration among teams and their fan bases this season. The rules around targeting are rooted in concern for players' safety — both the player making the tackle and on the receiving end. But that doesn't mean everyone fully understands the rules. So as targeting calls seem to evolve in turn with the college football landscape, what do this year’s targeting penalties look like? And what is targeting? We're here to break it down in simple terms. What Is Targeting? Targeting in college football, essentially, is when a player initiates forcible contact against an opponent beyond a routine legal tackle, block or play on the ball. And there's an emphasis around players' heads and necks. OK, so what does that actually look like? Targeting could mean a player leads with the crown of their helmet while making forcible contact OR it could mean making forcible contact above the shoulders of a defenseless opponent, especially with a helmet or shoulder. When a targeting call is up for debate by officials, it’s ruled a foul. However, there still needs to be at least one indicator of targeting. Some indicators of targeting — per the NCAA rulebook — include: If a player leads with the crown of their helmet, it’s targeting, regardless of whether the player is defenseless. Additionally, instant replays must confirm the targeting call because there is no "stands" option. What’s The Penalty For Targeting? In the past years, the penalty — in the second quarter of play — used to be an automatic disqualification for the rest of that game and first half of the following game. This season, the rules have shifted to allow fewer disqualifications. Now, if a player is ruled out for targeting in the second half, they do not face the first-half suspension. But, a second targeting that same season would force that player to face a first-half suspension the next game. However, if the player commits three or more targeting penalties, individual conferences have the option to submit an appeal. The appeal process includes a video review by the NCAA national coordinator of football officials. If the appeal is accepted, the player does not face a suspension and is eligible to play for the full game. Are Players Ejected For Targeting? Yes, players are ejected for targeting. A player will be ejected for the rest of the game if they commit a targeting foul. However, if a player commits the same penalty in the same season — specifically in the second half of a game — the player is ejected from the game and suspended from the first half of the next game. If a player commits three or more targeting fouls in the same season, they are ejected for the remainder of the game, and receive a one-game suspension for the following game. The suspension also includes postseason competition. The NCAA rulebook states the following: "As an experimental rule for 2026, for a player’s first targeting foul in a season, disqualification for the remainder of the game with no carryover disqualification. If a player receives a second targeting foul within the same season, disqualification for the remainder of the game and the first half of the team’s next scheduled game within that season, including post-season games." Targeting College Football Rule Changes Despite the minor changes to the penalties, the rule may only be in effect for one season as an experiment. "One of the biggest changes we've made for the good, once it goes to replay, you must confirm all aspects of targeting," NCAA secretary-rules editor for football and national coordinator of officials, Steve Shaw, said via CBS Sports. "This is an experimental rule this year and the commissioners were content (on that) they wanted to make sure this doesn't change behavior back and start a new trend of targeting."

articles.title: Coki y Yanguas, último obstáculo por el título para Galán y Chingotto
articles.standfirst: Los número dos disputarán la final contra Mike y Nieto en busca de recortar distancias con Coello y Tapia en el ranking
articles.summary: Los número dos disputarán la final contra Mike y Nieto en busca de recortar distancias con Coello y Tapia en el ranking
articles.body: El Comunidad de Madrid P1 ha discurrido como un torneo prolífico en sorpresas, pero tras una sucesión de marcadores inesperados durante la semana, la jornada de sábado en el Movistar Arena ha certificado el triunfo de los favoritos de cada cruce: Ale Galán y Fede Chingotto disputarán el título masculino frente a Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas. Los pupilos de Jorge Martínez tenían enfrente a Íñigo Jofre y Jairo Bautista, quienes venían completando un torneo sobresaliente tras eliminar a duplas como Momo González-Lucas Campagnolo o José Jiménez-Álex Arroyo. Sin embargo, el canario y el malagueño no pudieron prolongar su recorrido en la capital. A pesar de completar un choque de alto nivel y sostener el ritmo de Galán y Chingotto, los número dos exhibieron esa versión determinante que evitó contratiempos en la moqueta. Especialmente acertado se mostró el argentino en la diagonal, encontrando mejores sensaciones que en el duelo de cuartos de final ante Martín Di Nenno. El primer parcial se resolvió con un 6-3 que encarriló la clasificación de los segundos cabezas de serie. En la segunda manga, pese a un amago de reacción por parte de Bautista y Jofre que amenazó con ajustar el marcador, Galán y Chingotto abrocharon el billete a la final con un definitivo 6-4. Durante el curso 2025, Coki Nieto y Mike Yanguas firmaron una campaña marcada por la regularidad. Acumularon múltiples presencias en semifinales y comprometiendo a las primeras parejas del ranking, pero sin lograr el acceso al partido decisivo. En el primer torneo de esta nueva etapa juntos, el binomio español ha conseguido alcanzar la final que se les resistió durante la temporada anterior. Tras dejar en el camino a los número uno Coello y Tapia en la ronda de cuartos de final, Nieto e Yanguas debían revalidar su gran momento ante Tino Libaak y Gonza Alfonso. La pareja argentina alcanzaba la penúltima ronda tras superar a duplas de entidad como Leo Augsburger-Juan Lebrón y Flavio Abbate-Alonso Rodríguez. La primera manga se decantó del lado de los jugadores dirigidos por Maxi Grabiel por 6-4, favorecidos por las condiciones rápidas del pabellón madrileño. Nieto mantuvo el volumen de juego ofensivo y la pegada exhibida durante toda la semana para liderar el ataque de su pareja. En la segunda manga, tras salvar varias pelotas de set en contra, Yanguas y Nieto cerraron el encuentro en la muerte súbita por 7-6 para sellar su pase a la final del domingo.

articles.title: Meet Josh Hoover: What To Know About New Indiana Star Quarterback
articles.summary: Here's pertinent information about new Indiana Hoosiers quarterback Josh Hoover, who shined in the defending champion's season opener.
articles.body: "Efficient" is defined as being "productive of desired effects," especially "capable of producing desired results with little or no waste." A thesaurus says that Josh Hoover's debut for the Indiana Hoosiers suffices. Making his first start at quarterback for the defending-champion Hoosiers on Saturday afternoon against the North Texas Mean Green, Hoover threw for 231 yards and four touchdowns, posted a 285.0 passer rating and completed 81.2% of his passes (13 for 16). According to FOX Sports Research, it's the first time in the 21st century a quarterback threw for four-plus touchdowns in their first start for Indiana. Hoover even played through blood gushing out of his face following a second-quarter sack. "Our goal today was to come out, operate, just compete and play our game at a high level, not hurt ourselves and take advantage of the opportunities we got, and I thought we did that today," Hoover told FOX Sports Reporter Jenny Taft after the 52-16 Indiana win. "Obviously, there's going to be things to clean up, like there is every week, but I thought it was a good start for our guys. And I'm happy for everybody." So, who is the fifth-year senior quarterback? Josh Hoover's Recruiting Background Hoover, who grew up in Heath, Texas, was a consensus three-star recruit in the Class of 2022. He ranked 42nd among quarterbacks in his class, per 247Sports. Ironically, Hoover originally committed to play for Indiana in 2021 before ultimately going to TCU. Josh Hoover's TCU Stint Hoover transferred to Indiana in January after four years with the TCU Horned Frogs (2022-25). After sitting behind Max Duggan in TCU's run to the national championship in 2022, Hoover became the Horned Frogs' primary quarterback for three seasons in the wake of starter Chandler Morris suffering a knee injury in Oct. 2023. Last year (2025), Hoover totaled 3,472 passing yards, 29 passing touchdowns, 13 interceptions and a 153.4 passer rating, while completing 65.9% of his passes. Over Hoover's three seasons as TCU's starting quarterback, he averaged 3,209.0 passing yards, 23.7 passing touchdowns, 11.0 interceptions and a 147.8 passer rating per year, while completing 65.1% of his passes. The Horned Frogs went a combined 19-12 in the games Hoover started. Josh Hoover Continues Indiana Transfer Trend In each of Curt Cignetti's three seasons as Indiana's head coach (2024-26), the Hoosiers found their starting quarterback in the transfer portal, a pattern that Hoover's arrival continues. In 2024, Indiana had Ohio Bobcats transfer Kurtis Rourke under center for a season that saw the Hoosiers go 11-2 and reach the College Football Playoff. Rourke led the Big Ten with a 176.0 passer rating and was selected by the San Francisco 49ers in the seventh round of the 2025 NFL Draft. Then, Indiana turned to former California Golden Bears quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who went on to win the 2025 Heisman Trophy, lead the Hoosiers to their first-ever national championship and become the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL draft.

articles.title: Three keys for Northwestern football vs. South Dakota State
articles.summary: A simple roadmap to proving upset watchers wrong.
articles.body:
Northwestern kicks off the 2026 season with a matchup that carries a lot more weight than the Week 1 tune-ups of the rest of its Big Ten compatriots. South Dakota State isn't some cupcake off the FCS ranks looking to cash a paycheck. The Jackrabbits are ranked No. 2 in their subdivision, they won back-to-back national titles in 2022 and 2023 (in large part because of Zach Lujan, regardless of how his NU tenure went) and they just finished torching Stetson 70-7 in their own opener. On top of that, this is the debut of Chip Kelly as Northwestern's offensive coordinator and the first live snaps of Aidan Chiles' Wildcats career, all happening in a temporary stadium before the real Ryan Field opens up in October.

There's a lot on the table in this early-September Saturday night matchup. Here are the three keys for NU that could decide how this one goes:

1. Establish the run and spread the workload across the whole room

Chip Kelly has never been the coach who wants to throw the ball 40 times a game, and his track record backs that up everywhere he's gone, especially when you focus specifically on this decade. His 2022 UCLA offense set a school record at 503.6 total yards a game while leading the Pac-12 in rushing at 237.2 yards a contest, which was sixth nationally. The year before that his Bruins ranked 14th in the country on the ground. When he went to Ohio State in 2024, his physical run game behind Quinshon Judkins and TreVeyon Henderson established the identity that propelled the offense to a national title, ensuring they didn't have to constantly lean on the passing game to bail them out. Kelly himself put it simply this offseason, saying his approach starts with figuring out what his personnel does well and building around it. The RBs need to take this opportunity to give him something to figure out.

In any new offense, starting off with an emphasis on the ground game is a reasonable bet, but it's especially important with THIS one. If Northwestern is going to dispatch South Dakota State, it needs to do it on the backs of its running back room. Besides Griffin Wilde, there are two real strengths on this side of the ball right now, and neither one is Aidan Chiles just yet. The left side of the offensive line, with Grant Seagren, Ezomo Oratokhai and Jackson Carsello all lined up next to each other, projects as one of the better units in the conference, and the running back room behind them might be the deepest it's been in years.

Chiles' progression is obviously the key to whatever Northwestern wants to accomplish this season, but nobody needs to see that today. He's talented, but he's already played for two other programs before landing at Northwestern, and he's had less than a full offseason to get comfortable in Kelly's system. Nobody in Evanston needs him going 20-for-25 tonight for this to work. What he needs is a run game that keeps the offense on schedule and takes the pressure off him early, and Northwestern has the pieces to do exactly that.

Caleb Komolafe broke out in a real way last season, netting 1,001 all-purpose yards on 190 carries with 11 touchdowns, both the most by any back in the Braun era and the first time a Wildcat cracked 900 rushing yards since Evan Hull in 2021. Joe Himon II, one of the team's six captains this year, ran for 486 yards and caught 21 passes for another 118 last season. He's already shown he can handle a lead role himself, piling up 103 yards in their 2025 win at Penn State. Then there's Gavin Sawchuk, who many on our staff have tabbed as a breakout candidate himself. The guy ran for 486 yards and eight touchdowns last year. He also 1,463 career yards and 19 touchdowns total to his name between his time at Oklahoma and Florida State. David Braun said as much himself at Big Ten Media Days this summer, calling the running back room a real strength of the team with Komolafe, Himon and Sawchuk all sharing space in it, and that's not just coach-speak when the résumés back it up. If Northwestern wants control of this game early, it comes from rotating that depth in and wearing down an FCS front physically before it has a chance to adjust. Even if Komolafe eventually separates himself, in week one that happens by not asking one guy to do it all himself.

2. Take away Chase Mason's legs before he beats you with them

Chase Mason isn't just a name on the other sideline tonight. He's a 6-foot-4, 240-pound dual threat quarterback on the preseason Walter Payton Award (FCS OPOY) watch list, and even in a season cut short to nine starts by injury he led South Dakota State to an 8-1 record in those starts and accounted for 21 total touchdowns, 15 through the air and six more on the ground, while completing 64.9 percent of his throws for 2,005 yards. That resume alone is reason enough for Northwestern's front seven to circle his number all week.

What's worth watching closely is how little the Stetson tape actually tested him. South Dakota State piled up 628 yards of offense in that 70-7 win, but Mason himself only threw the ball 10 times all night, completing five for 157 yards and hitting a 73-yard touchdown on the very first snap of the season, and he barely had to move outside the pocket because Stetson's defense collapsed immediately while the Jackrabbit running backs did most of the damage on the ground. Northwestern hasn't actually seen him forced off schedule yet this season, which means the pressure the Wildcats generate tonight matters more than whatever coverage scheme they dial up behind it. Getting him moving laterally in the pocket is what turns a dangerous dual threat into an average one, since accuracy drops for any quarterback once he's on the move, talented or not.

And if Mason does break contain and picks up yards with his legs, Northwestern has more than one answer waiting for him. Robert Fitzgerald leads the way. He led the Big Ten in solo tackles last season with 70 and finished with 115 total tackles, an interception and four pass breakups, the kind of season that got him voted the program's No. 1 jersey by his own teammates, the highest honor Northwestern hands out. But he won't be the only one out there. Braydon Brus, another of the team's six captains, set career highs at linebacker a year ago with 81 tackles, 4.5 tackles for loss and 2.5 sacks, exactly the kind of player who can get to Mason before he ever has a chance to create anything. And if Mason does slip past the front seven, strong safety Damon Walters gives Fitzgerald more help than he had for most of last season. Walters earned All-Big Ten honors in 2024 before a season-ending injury wiped out most of his 2025, and he's back now to pair with Fitzgerald at the back end. If Mason gets loose, that group is built to turn it into a five-yard gain instead of a backbreaking one.

3. Respect South Dakota State, but don't undersell yourselves either

UMass took down Rutgers in incredible fashion on Thursday night, in Piscataway, as nearly 30-point underdogs. With no skin in the game, it is awesome to see a team that hadn't won a game in almost two years take down a Big Ten foe. That said, it is also a stark reminder of exactly what not to let happen, and it's something Northwestern cannot shrug off heading into a game against a team with two national championships to its name.

So yes, South Dakota State deserves real respect. The Jackrabbits won back-to-back FCS titles in 2022 and 2023, they've made the playoffs 14 straight years, and they've beaten FBS opponents before, taking down Kansas in 2015 and Colorado State in 2021. David Braun isn't the kind of coach who needs a reminder about any of that, and his players shouldn't either. But there's a difference between respecting an opponent and forgetting who you are, and Northwestern has the better coaching staff in this specific matchup, full stop, with an offensive coordinator who won a national title at Ohio State and took Oregon to a national championship game as a head coach. The Wildcats also have more talent at nearly every position than a program that, as good as it is at its level, is still playing a level down.

It would be easy for Northwestern to treat tonight like some kind of lesser occasion. It's non-conference, there's no marquee name on the other sideline that casual fans recognize, the students haven't even moved back to campus yet and the team is still playing in the temporary stadium instead of the finished product waiting across town. None of that should matter. A home game is still a home game, and Northwestern should still be the better team regardless of what's surrounding it. If anything, playing in the temporary setup by the lake might work in the Wildcats' favor more than against them, since this team already knows exactly how the wind off the water affects the passing and kicking game in a way the Jackrabbits have no way of preparing for.

Nobody needs to be told twice not to overlook South Dakota State. The real danger is spending so much energy on that warning that Northwestern forgets to just go be the better team it actually is.

articles.title: HUSKERS FOOTBALL Recap – The Lads Pull It Together: NEBRASKA 49 Ohio 21
articles.summary: After a rough start, the Huskers took control and pulled away for the big win.
articles.body:
Come halftime, the Huskers had battled back from an early deficit to take a 14-13 lead, but you didn't have to be Nostradamus to know what was waiting on social media.

And apologies to Jashear Whittington who might not yet be aware his cleansing of excess Gatorade made him a Twitter star around lunchtime.

Not all the first half grousings were as kind or funny.

The first quarter was not pretty and, I mean right from the jump. After a fair catch on the kickoff, Ohio's Nick Poulos found Riley Neer streaking by a stationary Jeremiah Charles and drilled him on target after which Neer took off untouched until Andrew Marshall ran him down at the Husker 7. Charles recovered to play a solid game after earning his first Blackshirt, but he looked a little starry eyed on play number one.

Marshall's hustle went for naught as Ohio quickly found the end zone for a 7-0 lead. The Huskers matched it when Jamar Rule took it in from a yard out after a 75-yard drive, but the Bobcats would prove pesky and drive back into field goal range on their next possession to take a 10-7 lead into the 2nd quarter. They outgained the Huskers 138-84 yards in the first.

The Huskers actually flipped it on Ohio 139-52 in the second and began to take control although the scoreboard wasn't quite showing it yet. After that 1st quarter, Nebraska held a 439-167 advantage to make it a 523-303 yardage win for the game.

After a second Ohio field goal put them up 13-7, Nyziah Hunter decided to take a run with a kickoff right on the goal line, much to the dismay of the 411th consecutive sellout crowd. The dismay only deepened when he took it left to about the 20, then decided try and dip back about 12 yards in an effort to wheel it back around all the way to the right.

This strategy proved highly ineffective as he appeared to run out gas a bit, and yada-yada-yada, the Huskers found themselves starting from their own 8 as Husker Nation's Twitter fingers started loosening up as they braced for the worst.

Instead, Anthony Colandrea led the Huskers 92 yards in 7 plays going 3-4 for 68 yards with 24-yard TD pass to Rule. He also had completions of over 20 yards to Kwazi Gilmer and another to Rule on the drive. They almost tacked on another touchdown when Nyziah Hunter took a short pass and roared 57 yards for an apparent touchdown.

Except some more of the selective refereeing which has become so commonplace struck again as Jacory Barney was whistled for a shoulder to shoulder nudge deemed too far behind the play and 15 yards were deducted from the point of contact and the score remained 14-13.

The opening of the second half did not inspire confidence as the Huskers chose to lose 21 yards in two plays, including an 18-yard sack of Colanadrea, to flip the field position battle squarely in the Bobcats favor. They moved into field goal range and lined up to take the lead – and missed.

No one could truly know it at the time, but Ohio had just squandered their last chance to keep the back and forth going and how.

What Nebraska did was proceed to go over, around and through the Bobcats for the remainder of the game. They had five more drives and finished every one of them in the end zone. They went for 73, 69, 75, 70 and 17 yards respectively. The reason for the short pop at the end was Rex Guthrie snagging a tipped pass from the Bobcat backup QB and bringing it back 34 yards.

Colandrea, Mekhi Nelson (twice!), Rule (a third time!) and Kwazi Gilmer all notched scores as the Big Red tallied 35 second half points to pull away and cover a spread which was looking pretty safe on the Ohio side of things for awhile. The Bobcats managed one 2nd half touchdown, but it was the only score they could in their last 8 tries after finding points on their first three.

An opening game is very seldom high quality and, of course, there was good and bad in the Huskers' Saturday effort.

500+ yards was a fine start and this Husker offense truly felt like it was from the Dana Holgorsen construct. Colandrea was 18-32 for 275 yards and no picks with 3 touchdowns through the air. He added another on the ground while carrying it 8 times for 48 yards at 6.0 per clip (sack adjusted). His ability to scramble from trouble to positive yards was a skill probably not lost on the Husker faithful.

Jacory Barney Jr and Kwazi Gilmer were Anthony's favorite targets with 5 grabs each, but, to be fair, the passing numbers should have been better. Along with questionable penalty on Barney, there were several drops, something which must be cleaned up quickly.

On the rushing side, the backs gained 270 yards on 40 carries (sack-adjusted), a sparkling 6.8 YPC. Mekhi Nelson carried 10 times for 64 yards and added 65 yards receiving on 2 grabs for 129 total yards. You already know about his 2 touchdowns.

But the story today was probably true freshman Jamal Rule who rushed 15-122 yards at 8.1 YPC and hauled in a pair of catches himself for 47 more yards. His 169 total yards led the team as did his 3 scores. A 3-star recruit from Salisbury, NC, he looks like the odds-on favorite from his class to be one of the bigger steals of the 2026 group.

Not that I want to go too crazy or too quickly or anything. The coaches had told us since the spring he was special and doubled down on him this fall saying he would be right there with the top backs then putting him out there and letting him rip.

Last year's Achilles heel, the defensive line, held their own. Poulos found some scrambling room for 70 yards but the other back were held to 69 yards on 23 totes. They only managed 2 sacks, but were close several other times. We didn't need to see an instant turnaround in their fortunes in the opener, just signs of improvement and we may have gotten that.

Jamir Conn led everyone with 8 tackles, 4 solo. Riley van Poppel got one of the sacks. You heard about Guthrie's pick, and he looked FAST while he was running that sucker back. Donovan Jones also ran at blaze level and broke up two passes. Dexter Foster, who surprised some earning a co-#1 at LB, laid the smack down with 3 QB hits. And his partner, Vincent V9 Shavers grabbed 5 tackles of his own along with Guthrie.

After the shaky start, the Blackshirts wore the ebony proudly and the offense rewarded them by lighting up the scoreboard and the fans who had sweltered for a few hours. One had to imaging their gratitude after Nebraska opened the margin up enough to allow faithful to escape burn-off from the field surface which reportedly broke 150F.

The Huskers take on Bowling Green next weekend and the best news about that is a 6pm kickoff.

articles.title: How South Carolina football surprised Shane Beamer in hottest game in program history
articles.summary: South Carolina football played in the hottest temperatures in program history on Sept. 5 but Shane Beamer said the Gamecocks made it out injury free.
articles.body:
COLUMBIA — South Carolina football set a program record for hottest game in the 2026 opener.

At kickoff on Sept. 5 against Kent State , the temperature in Williams-Brice Stadium was 95 degrees, breaking the school record for hottest game by one degree. By the fourth quarter it reached 99 with temperatures that felt like 110 degrees, according to AccuWeather.

South Carolina won 57-0, with the lead already at 50 by the fourth quarter. So combined with the heat, the final quarter was shortened to 10 minutes. It reached 100 degrees with a thunderstorm rolling in by the time coach Shane Beamer got into the press conference.

The Gamecocks made it out injury and cramp free, Beamer said.

"To not have any heat issues ... it's remarkable," Beamer said, saying the word he'd use to describe his team was "rugged." "That's just who they are and they showed that today."

South Carolina football vs Kent State: LaNorris Sellers, Shane Beamer see top photos

The only South Carolina player who left the game was star wide receiver Nyck Harbor , but it was not related to the heat. He appeared to have bumped his helmet with a Kent State player's helmet while making a block. He didn't finish the drive with under two minutes until halftime but was on the field for the third quarter. He finished with five catches for 70 yards.

The athletic department, led by AD Jeremiah Donati , had large buckets of ice and water placed around the stadium and put extra fans on the concourse. Fans were able to bring in portable handheld fans.

By the fourth quarter, most students had left as the section is in the sun with zero shade but the remaining group was given free water. Donati and his staff rolled out large coolers and Donati went through handing out water bottles to students.

After the game, Beamer went over to high five the students who stayed the entire game.

"Thanks to our fans, they told me this was the hottest game in the history of South Carolina football out there today, and I've been part of some hot ones in Columbia," Beamer said. "Kudos to them, thanks to all of our EMS people."

South Carolina defensive back Judge Collier said there was "a little bit of a breeze" and it felt better playing than just standing, despite using more energy.

All week, the program said that the weather wouldn't impact the team because they practice in South Carolina heat every day.

"We're kind of used to it at this point," sophomore wide receiver Donovan Murph, who had a team-high 92 yards on four catches with two touchdowns. "When you're on the field, that adrenaline pumping, it's not that hot out there."

A crazy match at the Olimpico. Roma fired 36 shots and only managed to pull off a comeback in the final minutes against Atalanta.

After going behind early thanks to Ederson, the Giallorossi took the three points thanks to goals from Hermoso and Soulé.

Nahuel Molina, who came on in the second half for Emanuele Lulli, was also among the key players in the match.

The Argentine full-back spoke to Sky Sport: "The day I arrived, I found a team with a great desire to work and grow together. They've been working well since last season; I found a team with a great desire."

On possible similarities between Gasperini and Simeone: "Yes and no. All coaches have different things going for them, it's hard to find similarities. I found a coach with clear ideas, and I'm happy with him. From day one, he made me happy to be here; he immediately made me feel important. I'm happy with this new experience; I found a beautiful Roma team and a Stadio Olimpico that's always full."

On his many Argentine teammates at Roma: "It's wonderful to have so many Argentines on the team; in all the teams I've played for, like Udinese and Atlético Madrid, I've always had plenty of them. Now here too, I'm lucky in that respect. It's wonderful because you make friends and everything is easier, even joining the team."

articles.title: Justin Ishbia unveils his plan for a new White Sox ballpark on Railyards site along Chicago River
articles.summary: CHICAGO — Justin Ishbia’s vision of a new White Sox ballpark on the banks of the Chicago River in the South Loop was unveiled Saturday morning in a developme...
articles.body:
CHICAGO — Justin Ishbia's vision of a new White Sox ballpark on the banks of the Chicago River in the South Loop was unveiled Saturday morning in a development plan called the Railyards.

It's still a long way from coming to fruition, but renderings of the stadium at the Amtrak site across from the new Fire stadium show a packed, open-air venue with water taxi service on the river, a nearby Metra Station and a beautiful view of the Chicago skyline. The renderings don't show any parking, but a spokesman for Ishbia noted it's too early in the process and "all those issues and details will be ironed out if (the Sox) decide this is where we want to go."

Ishbia typically defers to White Sox Chairman Jerry Reinsdorf for questions regarding a future home for the team and won't reveal his own plans for running the club.

"My goal is to win," he said in a Chicago Tribune interview last year.

Reinsdorf has the option to sell his controlling stake in the team to Ishbia in 2029, while Ishbia has the option to purchase the Sox after the 2034 season if Reinsdorf opts to keep it until then. Some close to Reinsdorf have indicated he wants to be the Sox's owner in 2033, when MLB is expected to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the All-Star Game at Sox stadium, wherever that may be. The Sox hosted the first All-Star Game in 1933 at old Comiskey Park.

The lease for Rate Field ends in 2029, so Ishbia seemingly wants to get the ball rolling as soon as possible. Sources confirmed he would privately finance the new White Sox ballpark.

Ishbia met with Mayor Brandon Johnson on Friday, in what was described by a spokesperson as a heads-up to Johnson so he wouldn't learn the news through the media. Crain's Chicago Business reported on the development Saturday morning before a press release from Ishbia's developers, Canal Edge, was sent out.

Ishbia said in a statement the Railyards development, which would include a Northwestern Medicine health care facility, "is about turning idle land into opportunity — for patients who need better access to care, for a team and its fans who deserve a dynamic Riverfront home, and for a city that needs jobs, housing, and economic investment.

"This is a Chicago project, built by and for Chicagoans, and we are excited about its potential."

Reinsdorf previously released a plan for a potential new Sox ballpark at The 78, a site across from the 14th Street yard that Ishbia hopes to build in. That idea didn't gain any traction, but Ishbia's purchase of the property on the other side of the river spurred speculation that he intended to build there, and Saturday's news confirmed that.

A Sox spokesman said in a statement Saturday that Ishbia "recently approached us about his vision for the Canal Edge development which explores it being a possible future site for the next White Sox ballpark once our lease at the state-owned Rate Field ends.

"He agreed to conduct a multi-month study and evaluation of the site and to present those findings to the White Sox for consideration. If the site proves interesting and viable after his due diligence, it would be added to the locations up for consideration for a new ballpark, along with the 78 and other options."

A plan to move the Amtrak maintenance facility to Bridgeport has been met with community opposition, which could be an obstacle for Ishbia's Railyards plan. Ald. Nicole Lee of the 11th Ward is hoping to block the move, along with many residents who believe it would create noise pollution and lower property values.

Ishbia's spokesperson deferred to Amtrak on that issue, but obviously the Railyards development project assumes the decision will be resolved in their favor.

Along with the Amtrak issue, some residents simply don't want the Sox to leave Bridgeport. The baseball team has resided on the corner of 35th Street and Shields Avenue since the original Comiskey Park opened across the street from the current ballpark in 1910. The Sox opened their publicly funded stadium, then called New Comiskey Park, in 1991.

The ballpark wasn't a critical success due to its high upper deck and lack of retro features, but renovations over the years have made it more palatable. The lack of bars and restaurants within walking distance has been a constant complaint, and most Sox fans come to games and leave Bridgeport after it's over.

Staying in Bridgeport seems like a pipe dream at this point, and the question is where the Sox will go and how it will be funded.

Ishbia's involvement solves one of the biggest problems facing the Sox, as taxpayers are adamant about opposing subsidies for billionaires building new stadiums. The Bears' never-ending search for a new stadium is a perfect example of how Illinois taxpayers feel.

The Sox stadium is referred to as "The Railyard" in the renderings, though it likely would have corporate sponsorship. It faces toward the city skyline, unlike Rate Field, and a bird's-eye view rendering makes it look like Citi Field, the home of the New York Mets.

Ishbia's spokesperson said the actual architect has not been chosen and the renderings are a representation of a modern-day ballpark. It could look completely different if it gets built.

A few bridges over train tracks are shown that don't currently exist and a Metra station would also be built within walking distance, near the Northwestern facility.

The Sox are playing the Detroit Tigers in the rendering, a playful nod to Ishbia's favorite team growing up in Michigan. Ishbia has always said he's a fan of baseball, not just one team, and was seen last week in box seats at a Cubs-Brewers game at Wrigley Field.

These are heady days for the Sox, who are in position for a No. 2 seed in the American League postseason only two years after finishing with a major league record 121 losses. Reinsdorf's decision to promote Chris Getz to general manager was widely criticized in 2023, but Getz has built a young, blue-collar team that surprisingly leads the American League Central and is easy to root for. Manager Will Venable is on track for AL Manager of the Year, and rookies Munetaka Murakami, Sam Antonacci and Tristan Peters all have bright futures.

Reinsdorf has mostly remained out of the public eye, remaining in his suite at Rate Field and not made available to the media. But he's watched his Sox go from laughingstocks in 2024 to one of baseball's best stories in 2026. Unfortunately, the threat of an owners' lockout after the season could halt momentum if the 2027 season is not played, and he's long been a leader in the owners' quest to impose a salary cap.

The timing of the new ballpark release is curious, coming on a holiday weekend when people are enjoying their final summer vacations. But Ishbia wanted Sox fans to get excited about the possibilities — and certainly interest in the Sox is peaking as the postseason nears.

The Sox play a nationally televised game against the Minnesota Twins Sunday night on the South Side, and if the team gets into the postseason, the attention on their Cinderella season will increase exponentially.

articles.title: Dom Amore: Kalieb Osborne got into the end zone more ways than one in UConn debut: ‘Man, he’s crazy’
articles.summary: EAST HARTFORD — For a moment, Kalieb Osborne’s combination of confidence, exuberance and sheer athletic ability could have sent the whole UConn football seas...
articles.body:
EAST HARTFORD — For a moment, Kalieb Osborne's combination of confidence, exuberance and sheer athletic ability could have sent the whole UConn football season going the wrong way.

He was on his way to another touchdown, to extend the Huskies' lead to 42 points, when Osborne went airborne, hurdling defender Dhonte Jackson Jr. inside the 5-yard line and launching himself into the end zone.

"I don't know why he did all that, 'cause he was going to walk in and score," running back Cyncir Bowers said. "Kalieb? Man, he's crazy."

The overmatched Lafayette defense offered Osborne a blank canvas to paint his first UConn artwork, and he finished a museum piece Saturday. The Huskies piled up a school record 671 yards o f offense in their 56-7 season-opening rout, and 10 offensive series, a little more than a half of play. Osborne accounted for more than half of the yardage — 90 yards on eight rushes, 265 on 19-for-26 passing and four touchdowns, two through the air, one on the ground and one with his feet in the air.

"He's a tremendous athlete," said coach Jason Candle, a winner in his UConn debut. "Today, he was one of the better ones on the field, if not the best one. Once the ball is snapped, coaching's overrated, once they've got the ball in their hand. … Look, he's a pup, still. He's going to make mistakes, there are going to be some moments when you scratch your head. But there are going to be some other ones where you scratch your head and say, 'Oh, my God, what did I just see?'

"I would prefer he doesn't try to hurdle everybody from the 5-yard line, that's what I'd prefer. We'll get that figured out and fixed, too."

Earlier this week, Candle and the coaching staff made the decision that Osborne, who followed the head coach from Toledo to UConn through the transfer portal, would be the starter. Jake Merklinger, transfer from Tennessee, has a hand injury and was not available to play vs. Lafayette. Tucker McDonald, who has been in the UConn program four years, was the backup, going 6-for-7 for 105 yards and a touchdown in relief.

The going gets much tougher from here, when Maryland brings its Big Ten chops to Rentschler Field next Saturday, but right now this is Kalieb Osborne's show.

"Our coaches put me in the right spot and mindset going into this week and we had a great game plan," he said. "It was really just the preparation, trusting my teammates to be where they're supposed to be and trusting my O-line."

Osborne, 6 feet 4 and 218 pounds, looks like a true dual-threat quarterback, his running and throwing ability both high-level, which is rare. I will reveal that one scout, better known for developing women's basketball talent, attended a practice several months ago and came away talking superlatives about the plays he saw the kid from Toledo making. And how often is Geno Auriemma wrong? He was, in fact, on the sidelines enjoying the proceedings on Saturday.

Back at Waterford Mott High in Pontiac, Mich., in 2022, Osborne once accounted for nine touchdowns in a game, and it wasn't a meaningless rout; his team needed them all to win 77-63.

"That was a crazy experience," Osborne said. "I ain't going to lie, that was probably the craziest high school experience I had with that team. Such a great team. Today, I was just getting the feel of it, first game, first time out there with the new guys, so just playing every play my hardest."

A few months later, in March 2023, he committed to Toledo. After redshirting, he was a backup last season, getting to start the bowl game against Louisville after Candle left for UConn. So he had the most college game experience as UConn's three-man quarterback competition played out. After the first quarter Saturday, it looked like he could produce as many touchdowns as he wanted.

Right out of the opening kickoff, Osborne led the Huskies 75 yards in six plays, out of six different formations, and finished with a 24-yard laser to Javon Brown . His checked down to running back Kenji Christian for an 18-yard catch-and run on the next series to finish a 71-yard drive. He scored on the run before the end of the first quarter, nine yards through a lane about as wide open as wide open gets.

Osborne might've done even more damage before leaving the game, but the Huskies had an 80-yard touchdown called back for a holding penalty, and Osborne, hammered for one of the few times in the pocket, threw an interception. As it was, they scored on seven of 10 possessions with Osborne in the game.

He left the game after touchdown No. 7. The Hurdle.

"Going down the sidelines at the beginning of the drive I had a little run," Osborne said. "(Jackson) got kind of low on me and I stiff-armed him. I was having a lot of fun out there being away from the game for so long, so it was just instincts, I just jumped. I don't know why."

It's hard to take away much from a blowout against an FCS opponent, now that the days in which such teams gave UConn trouble seem like a distant memory. Next week, the defenders will close faster, hit harder, will be more sure-handed in their tackling. Balls will have to be delivered into tighter coverage. Then we will learn a lot more about Jason Candle's Huskies, and the quarterback he chose.

But we do now the sheer talent here could be something special, if Osborne picks his spots a little better. After the last touchdown, teammates joined coaches in telling him to protect himself.

"I was like, 'Bro, come on now, we got a whole season to play," linebacker K'Von Sherman said. "'Don't be leaping like that.' … We've got to get him over to the baseball team, teach him how to slide a little bit."

The Seattle Seahawks are gearing up to take on the New England Patriots for a Week 1 rematch of Super Bowl LX from this past February. Seattle will look to begin defending their crown the same way they earned it: by defeating the Patriots.

In the Seahawks' triumphant 29-13 blowout win over New England, one of the key players was tight end AJ Barner. The former Michigan star, who was primarily a blocking tight end during his days with the Wolverines, caught the lone offensive touchdown for Seattle that night. According to Barner, he is feeling confident, both mentally and physically, regarding his health going into the 2026 season.

Barner was asked about his health during a post practice press conference, and he gave an answer that every 12th Man will want to hear.

Barner is a critical cog in the Seahawks' offensive machine, and expect him to have an increased role as he enters his third season. Seattle's big man caught 52 receptions for 519 yards and six touchdowns last season - improving in all categories from his rookie year. With new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury's background in coaching the San Francisco 49ers' tight ends for the last several seasons, you simply must figure that Barner is in line for plenty of targets again this season.

Seattle kicks off on Wednesday night against New England on NBC at 5:20 pm Pacific Time.

articles.title: Cincinnati Reds vs. Milwaukee Brewers – Andrew Abbott vs. Dustin May
articles.summary: Can the Reds get a win over the mighty Brewers?
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers do not do very many things poorly. With 88 wins to their credit already in the 2026 regular season, they have logged 4 more wins than any other club in the sport, and they've done so with a precision-blend of talent evaluation and development.

Quite frankly, they're the model franchise for every other MLB club out there.

If there's one thing they may regret, though, it's the acquisition at the trade deadline of one Dustin May. So far, he's been shelled for 14 ER in just 19.2 IP for them since coming over from the St. Louis Cardinals, though perhaps the latter is all they really got him for anyway. They don't need him for the postseason, they just need him to keep as many innings off the other arms they've got to get them there.

May will start for the Beers on Saturday night in Great American Ball Park as the Cincinnati Reds once again play host to their division 'rivals' even though said rivalry has been hilariously one-sided for quite some time. Andrew Abbott will start for Cincinnati looking to reverse course on his own awful run of form – he's pitched to a 6.89 ERA with 24 ER in 31.1 IP since the start of August.

articles.title: Marquette explodes on offense in 69-45 victory over Kettle Moraine
articles.summary: Marquette produced 648 total yards, with 316 passing, 332 rushing and eight touchdowns.
articles.body:
Marquette's offense was too much for Kettle Moraine in a 69-45 nonconference high school football victory at Hart Park on Friday night, Sept. 4.

Marquette produced 648 total yards, with 316 passing, 332 rushing and eight touchdowns. Senior quarterback Ben Schroeder had 316 yards and five touchdowns. Sophomore running back Bear Bonk rumbled for 255 yards and three touchdowns. Senior Christian Miller was Schroeder's top target, catching four passes for 111 yards and a touchdown.

The Hilltoppers (2-1) also made big plays defensively. Atticus Godfrey helped hold things together along the defensive line, keeping Kettle Moraine (0-3) from establishing its offense. Caleb Miller intercepted two passes for Marquette.

Kettle Moraine also generated turnovers, intercepting a pass to open the game and picking off another to start the second half. A late third-quarter, tip-drill interception added another momentum-changing play in a game that featured turnovers from both sides. Junior Jett Allen was a defensive leader for the Hilltoppers with 16 total tackles, including two tackles for loss, along with a fumble recovery.

Kettle Moraine was led offensively by senior Nico Yttre, who had 291 rushing yards and one touchdown.

Marquette plays Franklin Sept. 11, and Kettle Moraine takes on Sussex Hamilton looking for its first win.

The Los Angeles Dodgers are hoping to keep the good times rolling against the Washington Nationals, looking for their third straight win.

Ohtani is nursing bicep and neck soreness, according to Dave Roberts, along with a sore knee from his work as a pitcher.

Dalton Rushing gets his first start since coming back from the injured list, stepping up into the designated hitter role.

Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernandez also get bumped up thanks to their form.

The key hitters include Freeman, Muncy, Tucker, and Rushing, the four of whom are the names to watch given their recent success and roles in the offense.

Glasnow is taking the bump again for the Dodgerse in his third start since coming back from the IL. Overall, he has looked sharp, but he has not been overwhelmingly dominant yet.

For a cerebral pitcher who has quite a bit of moving pieces in his delivery, Glasnow will take more time than most to get his mechanics in sync, but for the most part, he looks fantastic for someone who missed multiple months of action.

articles.title: Vincent Kompany explains Harry Kane and Michael Olise rotation after Bayern draw 0-0 at Schalke
articles.summary: Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany offered plenty of praise for newly promoted Schalke 04 after the German record champions were held to a 0-0 draw in...
articles.body:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany offered plenty of praise for newly promoted Schalke 04 after the German record champions were held to a 0-0 draw in Gelsenkirchen on Saturday evening.

Bayern controlled most of the match and created the clearer opportunities, but found Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius in inspired form . Kompany felt Schalke deserved considerable credit for surviving the pressure.

"It was a beautiful football match with emotion and passion," the Bayern trainer said at his post-match press conference. "There were also plenty of defensive situations in which something special always had to happen. Schalke managed that this evening, so congratulations. They did a great job and gave everything. You could see that."

Kompany: Bayern failed to sustain pressure

The Belgian nevertheless identified one clear deficiency in his own side's performance. Bayern enjoyed overwhelming territorial superiority, while Schalke rarely threatened at the opposite end. Kompany felt his team failed to maintain the tempo required to eventually break down such a compact defensive block.

"Every game has its own story," Kompany said. "Our story was that we didn't score and the opponent went home without a shot. But that shouldn't take anything away from Schalke. I've seen games like this plenty of times. You need 90 minutes of pressure against defenses like this until they crack. We didn't quite manage that today because we took the tempo out of the game several times. We only managed it for 60 or 70 minutes."

The scoreless draw ended an extraordinary Bayern sequence. The reigning German double winners had scored in 58 consecutive competitive matches since a 2-0 Club World Cup quarterfinal defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in July 2025.

Kompany explains Harry Kane and Michael Olise bench roles

Bayern began the match without two of their most important attacking players. Kane and Olise both started on the bench before entering during the second half. Kompany stressed that the decision had nothing to do with form or tactical dissatisfaction.

"The decision with Michael and Harry was simply completely rational," Kompany explained. "The two of them only came back very, very late from their holiday after the World Cup. It's not a given that you can just say: 'You play 90 minutes, 90 minutes, 90 minutes.' The cup match in Osnabrück [on Wednesday] also took energy. You can't always put that full workload on these guys."

Both players increased Bayern's attacking threat after entering.

Olise quickly forced Karius into a save from a tight angle, while Kane came closest to breaking the deadlock late on when his powerful long-range effort was spectacularly turned away by the Schalke keeper.

articles.title: Red Sox lineup: Three regulars not starting vs. O's on Saturday
articles.summary: Three regulars are not in the Red Sox lineup against the Baltimore Orioles on Saturday.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE — Three regulars are not in the Red Sox lineup against the Baltimore Orioles on Saturday.

Catcher Adley Rutschman , third baseman Caleb Durbin and center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela are not starting.

The Red Sox and Orioles will play the third game of this four-game series at 7:05 p.m. Right-hander Sonny Gray (16-4, 2.82 ERA) will start for Boston, while righty Chris Bassitt (6-4, 4.97 ERA) will pitch for Baltimore.

Rafaela is dealing with a tight right quad muscle. This is the third straight game he will miss.

Rafaela did not hit again today. The Red Sox are still looking to avoid an IL stint "at this point," interim manager Chad Tracy said.

"But I want to talk through the timetable on what that looks like as far as timing coming back," Tracy added. "And we have to discuss that. But as of right now, no."

Rutschman has been managing an elbow issue . He hyperextended his right elbow on an aggressive swing in Miami on Aug. 24.

Backup catcher Connor Wong and Gray have worked well together this season, but Tracy said this is not about pairing the two together.

"It has nothing to do with that," Tracy said. "Rush is fine. It's more like we're trying to make sure we take care of that thing. He's looked good and felt good these last two days as far as that elbow."

Tracy said the Red Sox don't want to push Rutschman too much and risk the elbow tightness "creeping up again."

"Get him back in there tomorrow," Tracy said. "So just being smart about where he's at with his elbow and letting him continue treatment and try to get us on the other side of that thing."

The Red Sox have a 1:35 p.m. game Sunday, a quick turnaround after Saturday's night game.

"Whether it was today or tomorrow, Connor was going to play one of these. So doing it today instead of tomorrow is all it is," Tracy said.

Durbin has looked tired recently and could use a couple of days off. He's 6-for-40 (.150) with a .292 on-base percentage and no extra-base hits over his past 13 games.

"Needs a day," Tracy said. "He just needs a breather. That's all it is. I just want to give him a breather."

Nick Sogard will play at third base and Isiah Kiner-Falefa will play at second base.

Eli White will start in place of Rafaela in center field for the third straight game.

Shortstop Trevor Story will bat cleanup.

articles.title: Oregon State football shows positives in opening loss to Houston
articles.summary: Oregon State football lost 33-20 to No. 24 Houston in the opening game of the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Beavers opened their season Sept. 5 at No. 24 Houston , falling 33-20 in the opening game of the JaMarcus Shephard era.

It's the second year in a row the Beavers lost their opener.

This season's first-game loss feels a bit different, though. A late comeback push and a flurry of youth finding ways to impact the contest with Houston — especially on the offensive side of the ball — leave Oregon State with several positive takeaways.

Sophomore starting quarterback Braden Atkinson delivered a stellar performance in his OSU debut. He completed 29 of 48 passes for 376 yards and a touchdown. Atkinson flashed capabilities in both the pass and the scramble, showing Oregon State fans a bit of what might come as a gunslinger.

"I thought that he did a pretty dang good job of just being a leader out there on the football field," Shephard said of Atkinson. "He was calm, he didn't change his demeanor the whole time ... very proud of how he led our football team."

Oregon State's 13 second-half points featured two pass-heavy drives from Atkinson as he moved the ball sideline to sideline, end zone to end zone. Both drives were over 75 yards and both were under six minutes.

"He managed the game in a way that I was super proud of him" Shephard said.

Nine different Beavers caught passes from Atkinson, but his top target Saturday was true freshman wide receiver Jesse Legree.

Legree posted 136 receiving yards on five catches with a touchdown in his first game as a Beaver. He excelled in the open field with his speed and evasiveness and is a major component of a young, exciting receiving corps in Corvallis.

"He's been a dog all fall camp," Atkinson said of Legree. "(Shephard) being our head coach being receiver-minded, we're going to have a bunch of explosiveness, explosive targets. We've got a bunch of guys that can run, can catch, make plays. My job is really just trying to get them the ball, don't be too cute, just try and give them the ball and let them play their game."

Additional offensive contributors include sophomore receiver Aeryn Hampton, who gathered 28 yards on four catches and freshman running back Kourdey Glass, who led OSU rushers with 25 yards on six attempts.

Freshman wide receiver Cynai Thomas also came up with some important third-down catches, garnering a total of 36 yards on two catches.

In totality, the offense wasn't as decisive or executional as Shephard and the Beavers would have hoped in the opener. But there were several signs of positivity from an offense going against a Houston defense regarded as one of top in the country.

"At the end of the day we've got to learn how to finish," Shephard said. "We've got to finish tackles, we've got to finish plays, we've got to finish halves, we've got to finish the game, we've got to finish quarters, we've got to finish. We'll continue to push that narrative for our guys to finish in every aspect of the word finish."

Oregon State's defense, contrarily, never got a hold on the game in Houston.

Houston quarterback Connor Weigman, who was one of the most impactful quarterbacks in the pass-and-run game last fall, delivered much of the same Saturday. Weigman finished with 305 yards on 20-of-30 passing and both a passing and rushing touchdown.

Houston had three receivers gain more than 40 receiving yards, including all-conference receiver Amare Thomas, who posted 133 yards and a touchdown. Running back Makhi Hughes ran all over the field with 98 yards on 17 carries with a touchdown.

Oregon State's lines, on both sides of the ball, felt the strength of the Houston trenches. Atkinson was pressured more than Weigman throughout the majority of the contest, and Houston posted four sacks to OSU's one to show for it.

"The game of college football is really about two things — blocking and tackling. We've got to do a little bit better job as a coaching staff to get these guys to block and tackle better to give ourselves the best opportunity to win," Shephard said. "But I was very proud of how our players fought."

Houston was a strong opening challenge, but Oregon State's schedule doesn't lighten up in the immediate future.

Next week, the Beavers are booked to face Big-12 favorites Texas Tech at Reser Stadium in Corvallis. The Red Raiders are highly touted nationally and a year ago beat the Beavers 45-14 in Lubbock, Texas.

"Excited to be home, excited to be in Reser, just ready to go play some ball and bounce back," Atkinson said.

articles.title: Game Discussion: Milwaukee Brewers (88-54) @ Cincinnati Reds (67-74)
articles.summary: Dustin May faces Andrew Abbott in game two of the series
articles.body:
After a back-and-forth game last night, the Brewers are back in action as they continue their push to the playoffs. They can cut the division number down to 12 with a win in tonight's game.

Dustin May is on the mound and is going to be looking for a bounce-back game. After two strong starts to start his Brewers' career, he's had three outings to forget. His last one was 4 1/3 innings against the Rangers, here he allowed four runs on six hits and three walks with four strikeouts. He faced the Reds back on July 24th with the Cardinals, and allowed just one run in six innings with eight strikeouts. In his five Brewers' starts, he has a 6.41 ERA and 5.43 FIP in 19 2/3 innings. Overall this season, he has a 4.69 ERA and 3.49 FIP.

For the Reds, Andrew Abbott makes the start. He's been having a rough season, posting a 4.49 ERA and 4.80 FIP in 148 1/3 innings over 28 starts. The Brewers faced him back on July 1st, and he allowed two runs, five hits, and five walks in five innings with three strikeouts. This is his 10th career start against the Brewers. Over his previous nine starts (50 2/3 innings), he has a 3.73 ERA.

The Brewers are shifting around their lineup with the lefty on the mound. Jackson Chourio bats leadoff with Luis Lara behind him and William Contreras batting third as the DH. Andrew Vaughn and Garrett Mitchell bat fourth and fifth, and Joey Ortiz moves up to sixth in the lineup. Cooper Pratt, Gary Sánchez, and David Hamilton round out the lineup.

articles.title: Grading freshman QB Faizon Brandon in his Tennessee football debut vs Furman
articles.summary: Freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon made his Tennesse debut in the 2026 opener against Furman. Here's how we graded Brandon's performance.
articles.body:
Freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon accounted for five touchdowns in his Tennessee football debut against Furman at Neyland Stadium on Sept. 5.

It was nearly a flawless first performance. He became just the fourth UT quarterback since 1995 to record three TD passes and two TD runs in the same game. Joshua Dobbs (four times), Joe Milton and Justin Worley were the others.

Brandon also tied a UT freshman record with five TDs of any kind in a single game. Casey Clausen and Tyler Bray had five TD passes in 2000 and 2010, respectively.

Granted, the 18th-ranked Vols outmatched Furman, an FCS program. And it will get harder from here, as UT plays at Georgia Tech (0-1) on Sept. 12 (7 p.m. ET, ESPN).

But Brandon displayed all his tools as a dual-threat quarterback to excite the Vols about his future. He became the youngest quarterback to start a Tennessee game at 18 years, three months and four days. He was also the first true freshman to start a season opener since Brent Schaeffer in 2004.

Here's a quick rundown of Brandon's performance against Furman.

Tennessee football vs Furman in Faizon Brandon's debut: See our best photos

Brandon was 13-of-17 passing for 226 yards, three TDs and no interceptions. And he rushed for 68 yards and two TDs.

Brandon tossed a 17-yard pass to tight end Ethan Davis. And he connected with Mike Matthews on TD passes of 55 yards and 57 yards. Brandon had a 6-yard TD run on an option keeper and a 7-yard TD run on a quarterback draw.

Faizon Brandon's best: Opening TD with ease

Brandon had numerous good sequences, but a smooth opening drive was essential for the freshman. He completed 4 of 5 passes for 43 yards on his first possession, including a 17-yarder to Matthews on an out route. Then he shuffled with ease through traffic for a 12-yard run.

Brandon capped the drive by tossing a 17-yard TD pass to Davis over the middle, a high-priority area for UT's passing attack. He showed his wide-ranging skillset as a passer and runner to start the game. From there, he just added quality plays.

Of course, the two deep passes to Matthews made for great highlights. But how well Brandon started the game was significant to his debut performance.

Faizon Brandon's worst: Only the coaches know

Brandon wasn't off target on critical passes. He didn't turn the ball over. He didn't hold the ball too long to cause sacks.

Brandon undoubtedly made some mistakes. But they weren't obvious to the untrained eye. Those will appear when he reviews the game film with coaches.

Brandon didn't need a performance to flirt with the record book to introduce himself as the worthy starter. He needed to run the offense calmly and make wise decisions. But he did all the above.

Some of Brandon's best plays were when he tucked the ball and ran out of bounds for positive yardage rather than throw a pass into coverage. But he was also accurate on short high-percentage passes, which can't be taken for granted, and hit two deep balls with precision.

Plus, Brandon looked like a comfortable and willing runner. He showed off his speed in the open field, and he pushed with power at the goal line.
