articles.title: UW-Whitewater has dominant, record-setting season opener
articles.summary: UW-Whitewater opened its football season with a dominant victory.
articles.body:
The University of Wisconsin-Whitewater Warhawks started the football season with a comfortable 69-7 win – and set a few records along the way.

The Warhawks defeated Carleton College on Saturday, Sept. 5 in a nonconference game at Whitewater and set a team record for total yards, with 762.

Senior Darrick Hill from Stoughton scored the first touchdown of the season for the Warhawks on a 98-yard run, setting a school record for the longest touchdown run.

The Warhawks got the ball back after the Knights punted and quarterback Justin Klinkner connected with Jacques Brooks on a pass for an 84-yard touchdown.

The Knights answered on the next drive when quarterback Tyler Mastronardi found Tyler Dimond for a 37-yard touchdown to make it 14-7 in the middle of the first quarter.

From there, it was all Warhawks as they scored 55 unanswered points.

Klinkner completed 20 of 23 passes for 366 yards and five touchdowns, with one interception. Brooks had six receptions for 145 yards and three touchdowns. Hill ran for 129 yards on eight attempts, with one touchdown.

In 2025, the Warhawks had an 8-3 record and lost in the second round of the NCAA Division III playoffs.

articles.title: Max Verstappen factor emerges after George Russell misses out on Italian GP pole
articles.summary: George Russell will start the Italian GP from second on the grid after missing out on pole position to Pierre Gasly, with Max Verstappen emerging as a factor...
articles.body:
George Russell will start the Italian GP from second on the grid after missing out on pole position to Pierre Gasly, with Max Verstappen emerging as a factor in Mercedes' qualifying disappointment.

The Mercedes driver appeared to be in contention for pole at the Autodromo Nazionale Monza, but Gasly produced a superb final lap to claim the first pole of his Formula 1 career.

Russell's frustration was compounded by an incident involving Verstappen during the final runs, which Toto Wolff believes had a direct impact on his driver's lap time.

Toto Wolff points the finger at Max Verstappen

The Mercedes team principal felt Verstappen's actions caused the field to back up as the drivers prepared to begin their final attempts.

"Yeah, I think at the end," Wolff told Sky Sports F1. "Where he got done over by Max in the final run when launching the lap.

"It was just much too close, and that compromised the lap time eventually and that lost pole position."

Russell offered a more detailed account of what happened, claiming Verstappen braked heavily into Turn 11 rather than wanting to be the lead car.

"Everything was all looking fine but then going into Parabolica, Max just slammed on the brakes," Russell said. "And didn't want to be the lead car.

"In hindsight, it would probably have been better not trying this, but P2 is a good place to start."

The incident did not lead to an investigation, with Verstappen not being noted or summoned by the FIA.

As a result, the Red Bull driver will start Sunday's Italian GP from fifth, while Russell has to settle for second after Gasly's late qualifying effort denied Mercedes pole position.

For Russell, the outcome leaves him with a strong starting position, but Wolff's comments make clear that Mercedes believes Verstappen played a part in preventing them from taking the top spot.

articles.title: Central Michigan opens 2026 season at New Mexico in first-ever meeting between the schools
articles.summary: Central Michigan will begin its 2026 football season tonight against New Mexico at University Stadium in Albuquerque.
articles.body:
LANSING, Mich. (WLNS) — Central Michigan opens its 2026 football season tonight at New Mexico, the first meeting between the two programs in either school's history.

Kickoff at University Stadium in Albuquerque, New Mexico, is set for 10 p.m. Eastern Time and 8 p.m. local time on FS1.

The game starts the second season under Matt Drinkall, who took the Chippewas to a bowl game in his first year — the program's first postseason appearance since 2021. Central Michigan finished 7-6 overall and 5-3 in the Mid-American Conference, good for fifth place. League coaches picked CMU to finish fifth again in the 12-team MAC this year, the school said.

Drinkall said at MAC media day in July that he expects a more open approach this fall.

"We were incredibly conservative in all three phases," he said. "Now we'll be able to blossom out a little bit and expand and play a little bit more exciting football."

Both teams enter the night at 0-0, and both are also breaking in a quarterback.

Central Michigan lists senior Angel Flores and junior Jadyn Glasser as co-starters on its Week 1 depth chart, with senior Marcus Beamon behind them, according to the Albuquerque Journal. All three saw action last season.

The Chippewas return their leading receiver, senior Langston Lewis, who caught 43 passes for 596 yards and three touchdowns in 2025 and was named third-team All-MAC. Seniors Vaughn Blue and junior Brock Townsend are listed as co-starters at running back.

New Mexico is in a similar spot. Second-year head coach Jason Eck lists three quarterbacks — James Laubstein, Luke Moga and Toa Fa'avae — and told reporters he plans to rotate two or three of them tonight.

"One thing I like about playing multiple quarterbacks is — and I'm a big believer of this — playing a lot of guys if you have close battles, I think you build depth that way," Eck said.

Tonight's game replaces a road trip to New Mexico State that had been on Central Michigan's schedule for the same date, the second half of a home-and-home series that started in Mount Pleasant in 2019.

The Chippewas play their home opener Sept. 12 against Colgate, then host Wyoming on Sept. 19 before closing non-conference play at the University of Miami in Florida on Sept. 26.

articles.title: Katie Taylor vs. Flora Pili LIVE round-by-round updates
articles.summary: Katie Taylor faces Floria Pili in Taylor’s final fight of her career
articles.body:
MMA Fighting has Katie Taylor vs. Flora Pili live round-by-round updates for one of the most anticipated boxing fights of the year at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday afternoon.

The main event is expected to begin around 5 p.m. on DAZN pay-per-videw. Check out our Taylor vs. Pili results page to find out what happened on the undercard.

Katie Taylor (25-1) has reeled off three straight wins since her lone career loss. She is looking to leave the sport with her third undisputed title in her legendary career.

Flora Pili (12-0) has yet to taste defeat in her career. Pili defeated Jelena Janicijevic via majority decision to win the IBO super lightweight title in her last outing this past December.

Check out the Taylor vs. Pili round-by-round live blog below.

Pretty sweet promo package featuring Barry Keoghan, and we're moments away from walkouts.

And by moments away, I mean we have a gorgeous performance of Grace and then anthems.

Out first, the undisputed challenger, Flora Pili.

And now, Katie Taylor. Absolute chills. Just incredible work to honor the boxing legend throughout the card, and now it's her moment.

David Irving is your referee for the main event.

Taylor immediately takes the center of the ring and she's stalking Pili. Taylor works her way in with the jab and lands a solid right hook. That ring is getting small for the challenger. Taylor steps in with another quick combo. Pili looking to counter, but she's having trouble landing clean. Taylor jabs the body and she comfortably takes the opening round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor.

Taylor corners Pili seconds into the round. Definitely feels like Pili is a tad intimidated in there, though she works her way out. Now it's Taylor circling. She closes the distance and lands a four-punch combination. Not much to score from Pili so far. Quick right by Taylor. She lands and makes Pili miss. Right hook by Taylor. Cruising through two.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor. Overall, 20-18 Taylor.

Pili has no answers for Taylor's jab. The champion lands another right hook. Not much action in this round, but Taylor continuing to snipe away. Pili flurries, but Taylor quick to tie her up and put a stop to that. Taylor wins an uneventful round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor. Overall, 30-27 Taylor.

Pili looking more aggressive here, but a Taylor combo immediately gives her pause. Two big punches by Taylor, but Pili with good defense. Taylor keeps up the pressure and another combo connects. Just not a lot of output from Pili, though she's moving better than she did in the previous rounds. Getting more interesting.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor. Overall, 40-36 Taylor.

Taylor makes Pili pay for walking her down, smacking her with punches. Pili with some sloppy counters. Taylor with a considerable speed advantage. Credit to Pili for coming forward, she's not fighting to lose, but she is having a ton of difficulty getting a bead on Taylor. Left hook from Taylor to close the round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor. Overall, 50-45 Taylor.

Nice jab from Pili to start the round, popping Taylor's head back. She throws again and Taylor has to tie up. Taylor finding her rhythm again, two punches down the middle. She lets loose with another combo and Pili has to retreat. Counter right scores for Taylor. Pili's punches coming out slowly. Taylor catches Pili with a left to cap off another strong round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor. Overall, 60-54 Taylor.

Taylor rips the body. Referee warns Taylor about a headbutt. More fast hands from Taylor, Pili answering in the middle of a flurry, she's finally connecting. Taylor lands a left as she circles out of danger. Taylor with another quick shot.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Pili. Overall, 69-64 Taylor.

Pili again looks to corner Taylor. She's making it ugly, which could be her best path to find a much-needed finish. Taylor scores with a combination. Pili with a short right. Glancing right by Pili. Tayor lands a good jab. She just pushes her way out of the corner. Close round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Pili. Overall, 78-74 Taylor.

Taylor staying at the edge of Pili's jab. Quick flurry by Taylor, Pili avoided the worst of it. Slip by Taylor, quick glove check. Taylor sneaks in that quick right. They're keeping their distance in this round. Taylor goes body-head. They clinch up as we head to the final round.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor. Overall, 88-83 Taylor.

Crowd roaring as Taylor and Pili engage freely. They can sense the magnitude of this moment. Taylor with a right, but Pili having success with counters. Constant pressure from Taylor, she's leaving it all in there. Solid right by Taylor. Punches in bunches by the champion, one last thrill for the fans. Good scrap and Taylor should end her career with her hand raised.

MMA Fighting scores the round 10-9, Taylor. Overall, 98-92 Taylor.

Official result: Katie Taylor def. Flora Pili via unanimous decision (100-90 x2, 98-91)

"Croke Park, we did it," Taylor says. "We brought boxing back to Croke Park."

She thanks the fans for being with her throughout her career. LOUD "Katie" chant.

An emotional Taylor takes a moment to just bask in the adoration of the crowd, incredible scene.

She thanks her coaches for rekindling her love of the sport. She also shouts out her dad, and mom is in the ring! Amazing.

Taylor embraces her husband and is taking her time with this speech. Doesn't look like a single person has moved from their seat.

Eddie Hearn calls Taylor "the greatest Irish sportsperson of all time." He hands Taylor her gloves and she makes one final walk around the ring. The gloves are laid down in the middle of the ring along with her championship belts.

articles.summary: It was a tough top-of-the table clash in Paisley between Celtic and St Mirren, and it was the league leaders who went home with all three points thanks to a...
articles.body:
It was a tough top-of-the table clash in Paisley between Celtic and St Mirren, and it was the league leaders who went home with all three points thanks to a 2-1 victory.

Goals from Liam Scales and Yang gave Martin O'Neill's side the win and maintain the team's 100 per cent start to the Premiership campaign.

Speaking to CelticPlayer after the game, the Celtic manager said: "I'm naturally delighted to win the game, and coming from behind as well.

"We started the second half very, very strongly, and while people might think it was a matter of time, it wasn't really like that.

"But we score the goal and it sets us off greatly and we go on and win the game 2-1. We had a number of chances to really put it beyond them but, honestly, I didn't feel as if St Mirren were ever out of it.

"I'm delighted that we've won the game, which is what it's about, and we showed some sparkling moments in the match, some really driving counter-attacking play, where we were very strong.

"In fact, the winning goal for us, we broke and we've had four breaking on it. And Yang, who's leaving us now, has scored a really great goal."

articles.title: How Man Utd plan to compete at top with richer rivals
articles.summary: Manager Michael Carrick and chief executive Omar Berrada are united in their viewthat Manchester United can be successful despite the club's relatively low s...
articles.body:
Manchester United believe they can challenge for major honours despite being unable to match the spending power of their rivals.

United spent £148m on new players this summer, less than newly promoted Ipswich, the £300m-plus invested by Chelsea and Tottenham and the record £458m spent by Manchester City.

In their victory at Ipswich on Friday night, Liverpool fielded three players, Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz, who each cost more than £100m.

By contrast, United's most expensive signing this summer was Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a deal that could reach £70m, still £19m short of the club-record £89m they paid for Paul Pogba a decade ago.

Head coach Michael Carrick says money in itself is not the answer to building a successful side and is adamant the club can compete.

"I certainly feel we can," he said. "The challenge is getting the right dynamics, the right balance and the right group together; getting the best players in the group to enhance the rest. Whether you need experience, or some younger players."

There has been some criticism of United's transfer approach, with the lack of a left-back to compete with Luke Shaw and no striking support for Benjamin Sesko two areas highlighted.

Carrick has rejected the notion restrictions have been placed on summer spending by United's hierarchy.

"The actual amount of money I understand can be a big thing but it doesn't always have to be the answer," he said.

United can manage debt and compete for trophies, says Berrada

Has United's debt has restricted the club's spending power?

Questions about that issue were raised at the Fans Forum at the end of June and respected finance blogger Swiss Ramble estimated in September 2025 that United had paid £852m in interest alone since the Glazer family's takeover in 2005.

The club's latest quarterly figures showed total borrowings of £1.29bn, including outstanding transfer fees.

United also took on an additional £91.92m when refinancing bonds in June and are yet to outline how they will fund a proposed new stadium expected to cost more than £2bn.

The club's full year accounts to 30 June are due out in the next few weeks and will show the latest picture after a season without any European football.

Against that backdrop, fans continue to protest against the Glazers at virtually every match. Yet chief executive Omar Berrada insists the club can remain competitive while managing its debt and stadium ambitions, arguing United's challenge is to operate sustainably while continuing to compete for major trophies.

"We have shown that with debt, we can not only [be] profitable, but more importantly, win trophies," Berrada told the club's Fans Forum on 30 July,. "And our aim is to do that again.

"Our role as management is to be able to operate competitively with a financial structure that's sustainable.

"We also aspire to build a new stadium, but we have to do it in a way that allows us to continue being competitive.

"We need to stay very disciplined and continue to take the right decisions on the pitch and put us in a position where we can do everything, where we can sustain the debt, aspire to build a new stadium and importantly, try to win as many trophies as we can."

The arrivals of Baleba, Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa, plus the emergence of 19-year-old forward Shea Lacey leads Carrick to conclude his squad is in a better position now than when they ended last season, when they finished third after winning 12 of his 17 games in charge.

"Being at this club, you've got to strive to win," said Carrick.

"That's where we want to be, and we want to try and get to that on a consistent level.

"I don't like to keep looking back, but they know what it's taken to put that run together. Granted, there was one competition, and we need to do that an awful lot more this season, but we have strengthened the group, so we feel good about what's possible."

Whether that optimism is justified will become clearer over the coming months, but Carrick believes United have assembled a squad capable of challenging despite spending significantly less than many of their rivals.

articles.title: Charlotte Hornets announcer broadcasts college football kickoff
articles.summary: Charlotte Hornets broadcaster Eric Collins called a college football season-opener between Ohio and Nebraska.
articles.body:
Charlotte Hornets broadcaster Eric Collins is staying busy this offseason, calling plenty of different sporting events. Collins started his summer covering AUSL softball with CBS before broadcasting a Major League Baseball game between the Washington Nationals and the Texas Rangers. With college football kicking off, Collins called Saturday's game between Ohio and Nebraska.

Although the battle was a one-point game (14-13) heading to the half, Nebraska dominated the final 30 minutes of play, outscoring Ohio 35-8 and cruising to a 49-21 victory. During the contest, Collins provided fans with one of his signature calls on a 51-yard touchdown pass from Anthony Colandrea to Mekhi Nelson.

Having joined the Hornets in 2015, Collins has spent 11 seasons with the franchise, joining Dell Curry, who began broadcasting for the team in 2009 after spending 10 seasons with the Hornets during his playing career.

articles.title: Kevon Looney Speaks On Luka Doncic’s Leadership And State Of The Lakers After First Team Minicamp
articles.summary: Former Warriors champion praises Luka Doncic's leadership after first summer minicamp.
articles.body:
Critics are still split on how the Lakers stack up against the rest of the Western Conference. With the Thunder , Spurs , and Timberwolves widely viewed as the favorites, there's a growing sentiment that the Lakers still need a few more moves before they can truly compete for the title.

Still, there are early signs that the Lakers may be poised for another dominant regular season. Some such signs could be seen at Luka Doncic's minicamp this summer , which featured nearly every player on the roster. The event received glowing reviews from the team, including three-time champion Kevon Looney , who applauded Luka's display of leadership.

"Man, I've been in the league for a while, and that [trip to Slovenia] was my first time doing something like that. Going to somebody's country, bringing us out there, and spending that much time together. I never did that before," Looney said of Doncic during a recent interview with ESPN Radio's 'Mason & Ireland' podcast . He's a great player and a great leader. He likes to show what he can do on the court, and then we get to see his personality off the court. So it was great. We're going to follow him and run through a wall for him."

The Lakers moved like VIP's during the event, traveling in their own motorcade through the city and frequently stopping for autographs. While they spent time bonding through various activities, they also put in some work on the court to develop chemistry and ensure a smooth transition after a summer change .

Luka set the tone well with his leadership and planning, sending a message of unity and focus as he prepares for the upcoming season. Beyond Doncic , however, the Lakers have all the tools they need to succeed , and Looney believes they have a chance to go all the way.

"After going on that trip and spending time with Luka and getting to know the guys and playing pickup, playing five-on-five, I feel like we have a great chance," Looney added. "We have a lot of talent. We got high-end talent like Luka and AR, you always have a shot, and we have great role players and guys that got a chip on their shoulder, who want to prove themselves. I think we got a shot."

As a featured big man during the height of the Warriors dynasty, Looney knows what it takes to win, and he's seeing things on the Lakers that he never experienced with Golden State. How much that will translate into winning remains to be seen, but everyone seems committed to the same goal, and the vibes couldn't be better.

For Doncic, the pressure is on to lead this team to glory and prove that he's capable of being their franchise star for the next 10 years to come. With averages of 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds, and 8.3 assists per game last season, we know his game is reliable, and the Lakers will need everything he can give to meet expectations and become a formidable force in the West.

articles.title: Husker Volleyball Takes on Missouri at Wrigley on Sunday
articles.summary: This match is part of the Big Ten/SEC Challenge.
articles.body:
What a wild couple weeks it's been for the Husker Volleyball team.

Next up is MLB Stadium Wrigley Field. The Huskers will be playing baseball style in pinstripe uniforms.

Last NCAA Appearance: 2024- Lost in the Sweet Sixteen

Missouri is in their fourth year with coach Dawn Sullivan. She came to Mizzou in 2023 and was named SEC Coach of the Year. She then guided the Tigers to a Sweet Sixteen appearance in 2024. 2025 was a down season, and they are ready for a tough schedule in 2026.

Missouri and Nebraska met regularly when both were members of the Big Eight and then the Big 12. Nebraska. The two teams faced each other 75 times, with Nebraska winning 71 of the match ups. A 1977 match up had only two sets play and the two teams ended in a tie. The most recent match up between the two teams was in the second round of the 2023 NCAA tournament where the Huskers won in three sets. The last time the Tigers beat the Huskers was in October of 2003, when the Huskers were rated #1. It was the first time Missouri beat a #1 team.

Missouri got their season 2026 off to a 3-0 start before they fell to #25 Oregon in four sets at home on Tuesday.

This season the Tigers are led by junior middle blocker Lauren Larkin, a transfer from Utah State. Against Oregon she recorded 14 kills, while hitting .552. This follows a 10 kill performance while hitting .625 against Idaho last Saturday.

Junior Nina Mandovic controls the court as the starting setter. So far this season she has tallied 96- assists. Last season she recorded 173 assists and 51 digs while appearing in 18 games.

articles.title: Kansas State vs Nicholls: 2026 Game 1
articles.summary: The Collin Klein era kicks off this evening. Time to see what this new staff and updated roster can do.
articles.body:
We're ready to embark on not just another season of K-State football. 58 new players on the roster, a nearly complete revamp of the coaching staff. And the return of Collin Klein to the K-State sideline.

This is something many of us have talked about since his should-have-won-the-Heisman 2012 season, where Collin led K-State to a Big 12 title and one of the best seasons in school history. But it wasn't just his athletic ability. All season it was talked about how Collin was first player Snyder had that truly understood the depth of Snyder's offensive playbook, and was allowed to call his own audibles on the field. He was a leader on and off the field. And then after graduation and a visit to the NFL, he returned to the sidelines and worked his way up as an assistant.

So many times we ask "what if?" about a former player coaching. Too many times we've seen guys with K-State ties go on to have success elsewhere and not have a chance to come home. For the first time, the stars aligned for the Wildcats and our dream has come true. Collin Klein is home and leading the Kansas State football team as the head coach.

Now we have to see if the rest of our hopes and dreams can be realized.

Klein and the new staff brought in 58 new players, but will still lean on a core of strong players that Chris Klieman left him. Avery Johnson returns for his third year as starter. Joe Jackson is back to carry the ball. Garrett Oakley and Linkon Cure could be among the best tight ends in the nation. They'll work with new guys like Wendell Gregory, an All-Big 12 pick as a freshman last season at Oklahoma State.

The parts and pieces are there for a great season, but offensive line is a big early question mark after offseason injuries have taken their toll and will be a major story line to watch today. Time for the coaches to earn their paychecks, time for the players to step up and earn the money they're all getting from NIL.

Time to get out on the field and play some football.

We've got an 6:00pm CT kickoff from Bill Snyder Family Stadium being aired on ESPN+ with Mark Neely (play-by-play) and Jeff Woody (analysis) on the call.

If you haven't picked up ESPN+ yet the game can be heard across the 29-station K-State Sports Network with Wyatt Thompson (play-by-play), former K-State quarterback Stan Weber (analysis), and Matt Walters (sidelines) calling the action. The game will also be on SiriusXM Satellite Radio Ch. 173 or 238, and available online via the Varsity Network app . Live stats are also available at k-statesports.com, and Twitter updates (@KStateFB) will also be a part of the coverage.

articles.title: Wigan crush Leeds to move closer to winning shield
articles.summary: Wigan Warriors move within touching distance of winning the League Leaders' Shield after a superb victory at closest rivals Leeds Rhinos.
articles.body:
Tries: Keighran 3, Daniel, Marshall, French, Field Goals: Keighran 6

Wigan Warriors produced an outstanding display on the big occasion once again as they defeated Leeds Rhinos to take a giant step towards lifting the League Leaders' Shield.

The Warriors leapfrogged the Rhinos to move two points clear at the top and if they match Leeds' result in the final game of the regular season on Friday, they will claim their second piece of silverware of the year.

It was their 14th straight Super League win and it is hard to imagine them not beating Catalans Dragons at home to finish the job, with the Rhinos welcoming Hull FC at the same time.

Two early tries from Adam Keighran put them in charge at a sold-out Headingley before Ash Handley got Leeds on the scoreboard before the break.

Teenage winger Austin Daniel scored only his second Super League try to restore a 10-point advantage before fellow winger Liam Marshall crossed early in the second half to put Wigan firmly in control.

Their defence remained resolute as Leeds tried to get back into the game, and further tries from star backs Bevan French and Jai Field and a hat-trick from Keighran showed why they will be strong favourites to win the Grand Final at Old Trafford on 3 October.

The Rhinos have been top since May in pursuit of their first silverware since 2020 – a long wait for one of rugby league's powerhouses - while they have not finished top of Super League since 2015.

But the Warriors have been in their rearview mirror as they have been imperious through the summer, on the back of a winning streak which started more than three months ago with a dismantling of Hull KR in the Challenge Cup final at Wembley.

After a shaky spring, Wigan have been back to their best as they chase a treble, to go with the quadruple they secured two years ago.

Super League's leading try scorer, Maika Sivo, did not make the Leeds squad after recovering from a broken arm, but there was a setback for the hosts early in the game as full-back Lachie Miller limped off with a hamstring injury.

With the Rhinos reshuffling, Wigan pounced as the great teams do. Sharp handling from French and Keighran got the ball to teenage winger Austin Daniel who, on just his fourth league appearance, showed a turn of pace down the wing and then awareness to set up Keighran to score.

Oliver Partington had a try disallowed, but the Warriors were not to be denied as French's bullet pass put fellow Australian Keighran over again.

Leeds were stunned but found a response as Connor hoisted a high kick which was brilliantly caught and then touched down by captain Handley.

They were right back in the contest, but French simply dipped into his box of tricks to move Wigan further clear as the stand-off threw a sensational pass that took out three defenders and gave Daniel a walk-in.

Connor kicked a goal on the stroke of half-time to reduce the gap to eight points. But the visitors claimed the first score of the second half through Marshall's trademark finish in the left corner, although the unhappy hosts believed Wigan had knocked on in the build-up.

There was a hint of desperation as Leeds tried to force their way back into the game, but there were no chinks in the Warriors defence and their class was on show at the other end.

Harry Smith's clever kick found space and French, on his 200th career appearance, was first on to it, before Field's dazzling feet grabbed Wigan's sixth try.

Keighran then completed his hat-trick as the clock was ticking down to cap another glorious night for this storied club.

Leeds Rhinos head coach Brad Arthur told BBC Radio Leeds:

"We're disappointed, we didn't put our best foot forward tonight. It was a big occasion for the club and not through effort, but we let ourselves down and we let the club down.

"It's certainly not over, but we've got to dust ourselves down. We've got a big game next week and we need to regain some form.

On Lachlan Miller's injury: "It's not great. He's obviously got to go and have scans, but I think he's torn his hamstring. We'll have to wait and see.

"It's hard to replace a player of his quality, but then it's hard to replace a full-back, they're so integral to your defensive line, the organisation of that and how he returns the ball.

"We were a bit disjointed from it, but we've got to be a bit more resilient."

Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet told BBC Radio Manchester:

"I was pleased with the performance. I knew we were coming up against a really good team - a great arena, the build-up, the crowd.

"We knew it was going to be a big occasion, so to get the job done, I'm pleased, I'm proud.

"Leeds get the basics of the game right and challenge you in so many ways, so concentration is a big one and then embracing the big occasion. These are the sorts of games you want to be involved in as players."

articles.title: Luke Humphries beats Beau Greaves at Czech Open as Luke Littler also wins
articles.summary: Luke Humphries and Luke Littler came through their second round matches to progress at the Czech Open on the European Tour.
articles.body:
Luke Humphries and Luke Littler came through their second round matches to progress at the Czech Open on the European Tour.

Humphries ended the challenge of Beau Greaves, who had become the first woman to win a match on the European Tour with her first round win over Daryl Gurney.

The world number two averaged nearly 109 as he beat the three-time women's World Matchplay champion 6-2 in Prague.

"She's an amazing player, she pushed me all the way, it was a couple of bits towards the end of the match that got me through in the end," said Humphries, who will play Andrew Gilding in the third round.

"She's just a great dart player. If I had lost today, I wouldn't have been disgraced, I would have lost to a really great dart player."

World number one Littler had missed the last eight events on the European Tour and marked his return with a 6-4 victory against Germany's Niko Springer.

Littler, who won the men's World Matchplay title in July but was beaten by Brendan Dolan in the semi-finals of a Players Championship event last month, had a 108.59 average in his win.

"It's been a while since I've been to a European Tour," said Littler, who will next play Krzysztof Ratajski.

"Full credit to Niko. I was 5-2 up and then suddenly it was 5-4 and he was right back in it.

"I've just produced a 108 average, but when I was practising backstage I couldn't hit anything."

Michael van Gerwen and Gian van Veen also reached the last 16 with respective wins against Mario Vandenbogaerde and Jeffrey de Graaf.

articles.title: British Open: Jak Jones stuns Judd Trump to set up Mark Selby final
articles.summary: Jak Jones earns a surprise win against Judd Trump at the British Open, and will face Mark Selby in the final.
articles.body:
Jak Jones earned a surprise win against Judd Trump at the British Open and will face Mark Selby in the final.

Jones produced breaks of 95 and 68 on the way to a 3-1 lead before Trump levelled the match at 3-3.

However, Jones knocked in a 59 and a 52 to go 5-3 in front and, after England's Trump missed a green on the colours in a lengthy ninth frame, the Welshman secured victory.

"I started off quite well before the interval and then after that I started missing a few, didn't I?" Jones, beaten finalist in the 2024 World Championship, told Channel 5.

"I can't say I'm in this position a lot so it's a bit different for me compared to Judd."

Meanwhile, Selby came through a hard-fought win against fellow Englishman Liam Highfield, who was playing in his first ranking event semi-final.

Highfield took the opening frame before Selby levelled with an 85 and moved into a 3-2 lead.

A 56 helped Highfield level at 3-3, but Selby took three frames in a row to secure a 6-3 victory and a place in his 40th ranking event final.

"It was a tough match, Liam didn't make it easy for me at all," said Selby, who can climb from fourth to second in the rankings if he wins the title.

"His safety was incredible. I can't remember him playing a poor safety shot all the way through the match."

He added: "To think, when I was starting out, a 16-year-old kid in 1999, if somebody had said I'd get to 40 ranking finals, I'd have said 'no chance'. I'd have been happy to get to just one or two."

articles.title: Fan runs onto field at Houston Cougars game, gets absolutely trucked by police officer
articles.summary: A fan who rushed the field during the Houston Cougars’ 33-20 win over the Oregon State Beavers was leveled by a police officer with a textbook tackle.
articles.body: The college football season, in all its glory, is upon us, and it feels like it couldn’t have come soon enough for all of us. In fact, a lunatic in Houston couldn't wait more than one game before sprinting onto the field. Unfortunately for him — but fortunately for the rest of us — he was absolutely demolished by a police officer who was at the top of his game. HERE'S WHY, EVEN WITH ALL ITS PROBLEMS, COLLEGE FOOTBALL IS STILL BETTER THAN THE NFL The No. 23 Cougars opened their season with one of the tougher Week 1 matchups, with the Oregon State Beavers coming to town. Sure, you get a few moments of fleeting face time on social media, but at what cost? Legal problems? Expulsion? Getting driven through the Earth's crust by a cop or security guard who definitely played at least a year or two of college ball? articles.title: Drew Mestemaker, North Texas transfers fall short as Oklahoma State drops 24-10 stunner at Tulsa
articles.summary: Oklahoma State turned the ball over four times and dropped new coach Eric Morris' debut with the Cowboys.
articles.body:
TULSA, Okla. -- Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Caleb Hawkins had the hype.

Tulsa's Baylor Hayes and Damari Alston delivered the goods.

Hayes passed for 227 yards and a touchdown, Alston ran for 73 yards and two scores, and the Golden Hurricane upset the revamped Cowboys 24-10 on Saturday afternoon.

Oklahoma State was optimistic heading into the season. Mestemaker and Hawkins were the best of the players who joined coach Eric Morris in a mass exodus from a very successful North Texas program. The Cowboys have 21 players who played for Morris among 70 newcomers.

Despite all the changes and transfers, the Cowboys got roughly the same result against Tulsa as last year, when the Cowboys' loss to the the Golden Hurricane was the final straw that got longtime coach Mike Gundy fired. It's the first time since 1951 and 1952 that Tulsa has defeated Oklahoma State in consecutive years.

Tulsa had trouble putting Oklahoma State away, but the Cowboys helped.

Mestemaker threw an interception to Zach Williams in the end zone with just over four minutes remaining, then threw another interception in the final minute. The Cowboys turned the ball over four times and converted on just two of six fourth downs.

All was going well for the Cowboys until left tackle Jacob Sexton was carted off with a lower body injury in the first quarter. One of the Cowboys' three offensive captains, Sexton already had missed significant time in two previous seasons due to injury.

Mestemaker looked shaky in the first half, occasionally oveerthrowing receivers and having to deal with pressure throughout the first half.

Tulsa led 10-3 at halftime, and pushed the advantage to 17-3 on Oran Singleton's 21-yard touchdown pass from Hayes.

Mestemaker finally got it going late in the third quarter when he connected with Justin Bowick for a 16-yard touchdown that pulled the Cowboys within 17-10.

Mestemaker completed 29 of 49 passes for 241 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions. Hawkins, who set an FBS freshman record with 29 total touchdowns last season, finished with 79 yards on 18 carries.

It doesn't get easier for Oklahoma State -- the Cowboys host Oregon next Saturday.

articles.title: Jinxed? Bayern Munich dethroned from top of the table after a record 67 matchdays
articles.summary: FC Bayern had a rare off day against Schalke.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich dropped points early in the Bundesliga as Schalke 04 held off the record champions for a 0-0 draw. Vincent Kompany's bulldozing run of the league where his team have dominated the pole position for 67 consecutive matchdays has come to an end.

The Bavarians are currently at 4th position behind SC Freiburg, Der Klassiker rivals Borussia Dortmund and newly promoted SV Elversberg coming from Saarland, Germany.

Miron Muslić set up the home side to cut the passing lanes and force Bayern to contest for the ball every time they entered Schalke's third of the pitch. 18 interceptions by Muslić's men were the result of intelligent movement by the Royal Blues in anticipation of a Bavarian pass.

Schalke also showed that to trouble Bayern, you don't have to outplay them. You just need to be good at rushing them and forcing a duel and a decision at the same time. Bayern's wastefulness in front of goal, Schalke goalkeeper Loris Karius' heroics along with some poor luck saw all six big chances missed. The Veltins-Arena witnessed their team finally draw a point against Die Roten after nine years.

A humble apology for the folks who believe we jinxed the record by writing about it. If there was one team who I did not see bothering the record, it was Schalke against whom Bayern have a fantastic win ratio. But, here we are.

Anyway, it has been sometime since Bayern was hunting for the pole position and this opening should incentivize the other teams to keep the Bavarians from becoming the leaders of the pack again.

articles.title: Eric Winters stops Baylor’s 2-point try as Auburn prevails 17-16
articles.summary: Safety Eric Winters spared Auburn from a Week 1 upset, stopping Baylor inches short of a two-point conversion with nine seconds remaining on the clock and pr...
articles.body:
ATLANTA (AP) — Safety Eric Winters spared Auburn from a Week 1 upset, stopping Baylor inches short of a two-point conversion with nine seconds remaining on the clock and preserving the Tigers' 17-16 win on Saturday.

Quarterback Byrum Brown dodged a pile-up in the middle of the field and ran for an 11-yard touchdown with 3:21 remaining in the fourth, giving Auburn a 17-10 lead.

Baylor quarterback DJ Lagway saved his best drive of the day for last, finding Gavin Freeman 27 yards downfield on a crucial fourth down and then four plays later hit Freeman again for a 5-yard touchdown.

But Winters stopped tight end Matthew Klopfenstein short of the end zone on the two-point try and sealed Alex Golesh's first victory as coach of the Tigers.

In a matchup featuring two transfer quarterbacks making their debut, it quickly became a defensive battle.

Lagway's first drive for Baylor resulted in a lost fumble, which seven plays and 45 yards later, Auburn turned into a field goal to take an early lead.

The Florida transfer's next two drives resulted in an interception and a missed field goal. Auburn went three-and-out after both of them.

Auburn found the end zone with 3:21 remaining in the second quarter when Brown led a five-play, 57-yard drive culminating in a 15-yard rushing touchdown from Jeremiah Cobb.

Baylor promptly responded with its most efficient drive, going 75 yards in nine plays for a touchdown. Lagway connected with Louis Brown IV on a 14-yard touchdown pass, cutting the deficit to 10-7 before halftime.

Baylor capitalized off of an Auburn interception with a game-tying field goal midway through the fourth, and then Brown led the game-winning 10-play, 75-yard touchdown drive.

Brown finished 26-of-35 for 259 yards, with three interceptions, 27 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown.

Lagway was 27-of-54 for 333 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. Lagway connected with Freeman for 154 yards and a touchdown.

Auburn: The Tigers repeatedly fell short on given opportunities. Baylor gave Auburn the ball five times between failed fourth down conversions, a missed field goal, a fumble and an interception. Auburn generated just three points off of those turnovers, punting three times and tossing an interception directly after the other four.

Baylor: Coach Dave Aranda's philosophy on fourth down didn't change over the offseason. After finishing third in the FBS in fourth-down attempts during the 2025 season, Baylor went for it five times and converted three attempts.

Baylor hosts Prairie View A&M on Saturday.
